Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

mediamix 0.4.0.9000

Breaking changes

  • Recipes prepared with step_adstock() or step_saturation() by an earlier version must be prepared again; bake() stops on the old format. A prepared step_adstock() now stores each group’s training time points and media values (about 25 KB for mm_weekly).
  • tidy() on the recipe steps returns a tibble; an ungrouped adstock step shows group as NA, and step_saturation() shows NA for parameters its curve ignores. Keys for numeric and date-time by columns are written from their values (100000 rather than “1e+05”; date-times in UTC).
  • tune_carryover()’s metric field is the score; the metric’s name moved to metric_name, matching tune_carryover_joint(). std_err is the standard error of metric, so best_1se can differ from earlier versions, and half_life is NA for max_lag = 1.
  • tune_carryover() pools out-of-sample forecasts by default (aggregate = "pooled"), so its reported RMSE is a root mean squared forecast error. Per-split metrics used to be averaged, so with the default one-period assessment sets the reported “rmse” was a mean absolute error. aggregate = "mean" restores the previous averaging of per-split metrics.
  • adstock_state() returns an mm_adstock_state that records max_lag (and, for the infinite kernel, decay and kernel); the transforms refuse a state computed for another kernel. as.numeric() gives the bare value, and plain numbers are still accepted as state.
  • adstock_steady_state() stops on missing values by default (new na_action), rmse() and mae() stop on empty input, and block_bootstrap() stops when block_length covers a whole series.
  • Inputs that used to pass, or were altered without a message, now stop with a message naming the problem: text timestamps that do not parse completely, unrecognised conversion flags, missing values in controls, by columns or a step’s time index, infinite spend or state, constant or unnamed media columns in the tuners, repeated media names in diagnose_media(), spend text that is not a number, tol outside (0, 0.5) in step_adstock(), and overlapping journey ids under rbind().
  • build_paths() drops exact duplicate events by default (dedupe = TRUE) and sorts a conversion after touches that share its timestamp. On mm_events this gives 6,105 journeys (was 6,137).
  • block_bootstrap(by =) gives every group the same time blocks by default (panel = "shared"), so panel intervals change; unequal group sizes need index or panel = "independent".
  • contributions(), response_curve() and attribute() return subclassed data frames (mm_contributions, mm_response_curve, mm_attribution) so that plot() dispatches. Code that tests class(x) exactly needs updating.
  • plot() methods return their input invisibly. Bootstrap, contributions, response-curve and attribution plots used to return a modified data frame.
  • diagnose_media()’s CPM table names its row column row (it was period, but held a row number) and gains a group column when by is supplied.
  • mm_weekly spend and half-saturation points are rescaled by 1/20, so that average ROIs are between about 1 and 4 rather than 0.07, and coefficients and ROIs computed from it differ from 0.4.0. Decays and shapes are unchanged, and revenue moves only through rounding of the rescaled spend.

Bug fixes

  • The recipe steps, block_bootstrap() and diagnose_media() keep numeric group ids apart when they differ only beyond the 15th significant digit; such ids used to share one series, so carryover ran from one into the other.
  • build_paths(direct = "label") names a blank channel "(blank)", as "keep" and "drop" do, and an empty journey table keeps its timestamp class and settings, so bind_paths() and rbind() combine it with others.
  • contributions(by =) with a data frame of grouping columns labels each group with its values joined by " / ", and roi() reports the same labels.
  • Grouping by several columns no longer merges two groups when a value contains the character used to join the columns into one key; such values are refused with a message.
  • Error messages no longer suggest Inf for an argument that refuses it, and give an infinite bound as open when infinite values are refused.
  • rlang is now in Imports. Every error, warning and message goes through cli, which calls rlang, so without it installed even a warning stopped the call with “there is no package called ‘rlang’”.
  • build_paths() reads character timestamps completely: ISO 8601 with T or a space, fractional seconds and offsets such as Z or +02:00. Other text, or a column mixing dates and date-times, is an error. Such timestamps used to be cut to midnight, which reordered touches within a day.
  • build_paths() now reports when journeys hold several conversion events (possible under split_on = "none" or "gap"), since each is credited as one conversion.
  • dplyr verbs and rbind() keep journey tables valid: touch_rank, touch_n and the construction counts follow the rows, and functions that take a journey table recompute stale ranks with a message. New bind_paths() combines tables built by separate build_paths() calls.
  • Subsetting an mm_paths object so that part of a journey is removed now recomputes touch_rank and touch_n. Previously the stale ranks made credit_first(), credit_last() and credit_position() give some converting journeys no credit at all after, for example, filtering out one channel.
  • credit_time_decay(decay = 0) credits the most recent touch whatever the row order, and every rule sees journeys in touch_rank order. Character conversion flags are read as numbers first, numeric ids keep their digits, numeric timestamps record "index" units, and an NA row index no longer inserts rows of missing values.
  • media_transform() honours by inside the adstock list.
  • effective_window() is exact at whole half-life boundaries, transforms keep names and time-series attributes, saturate_exponential() keeps precision for small inputs, and fit_ols() keeps slopes at any scale.
  • The saturate-before-adstock warning and docs give the reason that applies to the kernel: with the default normalised kernel the result stays under the ceiling. The Markov null-path warning no longer claims every removal effect is overstated.
  • step_adstock() continues the filter exactly when new data repeats the end of the training data, as rsample::rolling_origin(lag =) assessment sets do; those rows were cold-started without a warning. A block that starts less than one period after a training time point warns (or errors under carry_over = "warm"), and the period is inferred within each group.
  • step_saturation() offers for tuning only the parameters its curve uses, and print() and tidy() accept tune() placeholders.
  • The tuners refuse missing controls instead of failing or shifting rows, compare every candidate on the splits all of them completed, warn at both edges of the searched grid, and quote the first failure of fit_fn, predict_fn or metric_fn. With cores > 1, one failing grid point no longer marks its neighbours as failed.
  • The one-standard-error rule compares each candidate with the reported best, using the standard error of the paired difference in the same metric. tune_carryover_joint() reports the error of its combined best_1se set as best_1se_metric.
  • warm_start seeds the filter only from media inside the first training window.
  • contributions() no longer applies the training fit’s fitted values to other rows (new newdata), keeps the controls in the baseline when the model dropped rows for missing values, matches back-ticked coefficient names, reports media columns that match no coefficient, warns for non-identity links, accepts one-row media and uses the fixed effects of nlme and lme4 models.
  • roi() and diagnose_media() read factor spend by its labels, roi() warns when contributions and spend cover different periods, and diagnose_media() flags CPM outliers when most CPMs are identical and accepts data.table input.
  • diagnose_media() now computes the implied-CPM median and outlier rule within each series when by is supplied. Pooled across geographies, a region that buys media at a different price was flagged as a stream of join errors.
  • mroi(), response_curve() and spend_for() accept type = "none", scale their derivative step to the curve and refuse targets no spend can reach.
  • The documentation and the getting-started vignette recommended computing marginal ROI on spend as the saturation slope times the kernel’s first weight. That counts only the period of spend and understated slow channels’ marginal return several-fold (six-fold for mm_weekly’s television), reversing a reallocation conclusion. See marginal_roi().
  • Plots: the joint-tuning plot draws one line per max_lag; the contributions chart sorts periods and labels date-times as dates; a missing contribution or share gives a warning instead of removing a channel; methods name any column they need that is missing.
  • block_bootstrap() draws every resample before calling the statistic (a statistic that set a seed made replicates repeat), sets seed before the point estimate, matches replicates by name, counts missing values per term and reports the first failure.
  • Group keys are type-stable (1e5 and 100000L are one group), a blank label is an ordinary group, and groups are ordered by first appearance, so seeded block_bootstrap(by =) results no longer depend on the locale.

New features

  • Budget planning from a per-channel spec, a named list of media_transform() arguments: transform_plan() transforms every channel of a plan, simulate_plan() reports each channel’s spend and predicted response (with baseline =, the change from another plan), reallocate() moves spend between two channels and keeps both channels’ flighting, and allocate_budget() splits a total across channels within per-channel bounds, by dynamic programming on a grid of spend levels, with a plot() method. marginal_roi(spec =) takes a data frame of spend and returns one row per channel.
  • from_robyn() converts one channel’s Robyn hyperparameters (geometric theta, Weibull CDF shape and scale, Hill alpha and gamma) into media_transform() arguments that reproduce Robyn’s transformed series. inflexion chooses Robyn’s Hill rule for version 3.12.0 and later, or for 3.7.0 to 3.11.1.
  • fourier_terms() and holiday_flags() build seasonality controls: sine and cosine pairs by time of year, and flags for the daily or weekly periods that contain a holiday.
  • step_adstock() gains Weibull and delayed kernels (kernel, shape, scale, type, peak), steady-state starts (start = "steady"), and keep_original_cols with prefix to keep the raw spend beside the adstocked column. step_adstock_channels() adds one step per channel, each with its own decay or its own tune() id, and carryover_shape(), carryover_scale() and carryover_peak() are the new kernels’ dials parameters.
  • diagnose_media(date =) checks each series for rows out of time order, repeated periods, missing periods and uneven steps.
  • roi() gains by, index and periods for returns by group and period.
  • block_bootstrap(cores =) evaluates replicates in parallel, with results that do not depend on cores. tune_carryover() and tune_carryover_joint() keep out-of-sample predictions with save_pred.
  • build_paths(keep =) carries other event columns, such as campaign, device or cost, into the journey table, and conversion_touch = "drop" stops the channel recorded on a conversion from counting as a touch.
  • attribute(by =) attributes each segment’s journeys separately, and attribute(times =, level =, seed =) adds percentile intervals on the shares from resampled journeys, with plot() methods for both. markov_removal() gains p_without and returns the fitted transition matrix as an attribute.
  • decay_from_half_life(), half_life() and effective_window() are vectorised over their first argument.
  • marginal_roi() computes average and marginal return by re-running carryover and saturation on a slightly larger budget, following Jin et al. (2017), with optional planning windows and carryover run-out.
  • tune_carryover_joint() tunes every channel’s carryover inside one model with controls, by coordinate descent, reporting each channel’s profile.
  • block_bootstrap(): moving block bootstrap (Künsch, 1989) with percentile intervals for ROI, marginal ROI or any statistic.
  • markov_removal() implements order-1 Markov removal-effect attribution (Anderl et al., 2016) exactly, in base R. attribute() includes it as the "markov" rule.
  • adstock_delayed() and adstock_weights_delayed() add the delayed-peak kernel of Jin et al. (2017); media_transform() accepts kernel = "delayed".
  • adstock_steady_state() seeds a filter at steady state, removing the start-up bias of long-carryover channels.
  • tune_carryover() reports std_err and a best_1se choice using a paired one-standard-error rule, and gains controls (entered into the model and kept aligned with every split) and warm_start.
  • by and index in tune_carryover() and tune_carryover_joint() tune a panel of geographies; se_block gives a block-jackknife standard error; tune_carryover_joint() gains cores.
  • diagnose_media(decay =) measures collinearity on adstocked media.
  • plot() methods for carryover profiles, joint tuning, bootstrap intervals, contributions (over time or in total), response curves (with the extrapolation region shaded) and attribution shares, in one colour-vision-checked style. mm_palette() exports the colours.
  • A plot() method for diagnose_media() results. plot() methods accept main, xlab, ylab and col, use k, M and B axis labels, and fold more than eight series into “Other” instead of dropping them.
  • as.data.frame() and tidy() methods for tune_carryover(), tune_carryover_joint(), diagnose_media() and block_bootstrap() results; coef(), fitted() and predict() without newdata for fit_ols().
  • contributions(newdata =); block_bootstrap(panel =, index =, circular =).
  • step_saturation(by =) gives each group its own reference level; step_adstock(period =) overrides the inferred spacing.
  • media_transform() accepts adstock = NULL or saturation = NULL to switch a stage off, and the adstock functions gain missing_state = "cold".
  • bind_paths(), and build_paths(timestamp_format =, dedupe =); path_summary() reports duplicate_events and journeys_before_filtering.
  • mm_weekly’s "truth" attribute records each geography’s scale factor and a per-geography table of channel parameters (by_geo), so a model fitted to any geography can be checked; the data are unchanged.
  • inst/CITATION added.

Performance

  • build_paths() is about four times faster (1.2 million events in about 2 s), assisted_conversions() is linear in journey length, markov_removal() solves all removal effects from one matrix inverse, tune_carryover_joint() is about four times faster, and grouped adstock and step_adstock()’s bake() are linear in the number of groups.
  • assisted_conversions() is about 16 times faster and top_paths() / as_channel_paths() about twice as fast on large journey tables, via data.table. response_curve() computes marginals in one vectorised pass.

Documentation

  • New articles: an index from tasks to functions, answers to common questions, and a guide to moving a Robyn model to mediamix, whose worked example reproduces Robyn’s transformed series.
  • The vignettes, articles and help pages were checked against the code. Numbers in prose are computed inline, claims about other tools cite their source, and the budget walkthrough, the getting-started vignette and the tidymodels vignette use the planning helpers and step_adstock_channels().
  • References carry a DOI wherever one exists.
  • The budget walkthrough checks its recommendation against the parameters the data was simulated from. The fitted model ranks the channels differently from the truth, and the article now presents the reallocation as a test rather than a finding. The getting-started vignette sets fitted marginal returns against true ones in the same way.
  • The tidymodels vignette’s per-channel loop used all_of(ch), which is evaluated after the loop ends, so all five steps adstocked display. It now uses all_of(!!ch) and prints what each step selects.
  • The methods article cites Tashman (2000) for rolling-origin evaluation; Bergmeir and Benítez (2012) recommend blocked cross-validation.
  • The README is knitted from README.Rmd, so its outputs and figures come from the code shown, and numbers in the vignettes’ prose are computed inline.
  • Claims corrected: dropping null paths does not inflate every removal effect; step_naomit() does not break tune_grid(); out-of-sample prediction is evidence of predictive value, not of a causal mechanism; and the joint tuner is closer to the truth than one-at-a-time tuning but not better for every channel.
  • README and vignette claims about other packages corrected: the README no longer says Robyn is not a CRAN package or that no other package builds journeys, and the normalised adstock kernel is now credited as the Jin et al. (2017) convention rather than a departure from the literature. The spine vignette no longer suggests an MMM half-life is an attribution lookback.
  • The README no longer tells users to install.packages("mediamix"); the package is not on CRAN.
  • A pkgdown site with an end-to-end budget walkthrough, a methods and references article and a comparison with other tools, deployed to GitHub Pages by a new workflow.

mediamix 0.4.0

First release.

Media transforms

  • adstock_geometric(), adstock_weibull(), adstock_filter() and adstock_state() apply carryover transforms with explicit, inspectable filter state, grouping via by=, and an explicit normalise argument whose consequence for coefficient interpretation is documented.
  • adstock_weights() and adstock_weights_weibull() expose the kernels directly.
  • saturate_hill(), saturate_exponential(), saturate_michaelis_menten(), saturate_power() and the saturate() dispatcher provide four diminishing-returns curves.
  • media_transform() composes carryover and saturation in the conventional order and warns rather than silently reversing it.
  • decay_from_half_life(), half_life() and effective_window() give both halves of the package one vocabulary.

Carryover selection

  • tune_carryover() selects (max_lag, decay) by cross-validation against an actual KPI using a user-supplied model, with forward-only resampling. It warns when the selected parameters sit on the edge of the search grid.
  • fit_ols(), rmse() and mae() provide working defaults.

Attribution

  • build_paths() constructs customer journeys from a raw event log, handling journey splitting, lookback windows, non-converting paths, direct and missing channel labels, consecutive duplicates, deterministic tie-breaking, and the accounting for conversions left unattributable by filtering.
  • credit_linear(), credit_first(), credit_last(), credit_position(), credit_time_decay() and credit_custom() assign credit; attribute() runs several rules at once and attribution_spread() reports how much the answer depends on the choice.
  • path_summary(), path_lengths(), channel_positions(), assisted_conversions(), top_paths(), conversion_lag() and path_diagnostics() describe the journey table.
  • as_channel_paths() exports journeys in ChannelAttribution’s format.

Recipe steps

  • step_adstock() and step_saturation() carry filter state across the train/test boundary without changing row count or order, classifying new data as contiguous, overlapping, gapped or unseen and warm-starting only when that is correct.
  • tunable() methods and the carryover_decay(), carryover_max_lag(), saturation_half_max() and saturation_shape() parameter objects support joint tuning with model hyperparameters.

Reporting and diagnostics

  • contributions(), roi(), mroi(), response_curve() and spend_for() turn a fitted model into a marketing mix deliverable.
  • diagnose_media() reports collinearity, insufficient variation, flighting and implied CPM inconsistency.

Data

  • mm_weekly, a synthetic weekly panel generated from known parameters.
  • mm_events, a synthetic touchpoint log containing the awkward cases on purpose.
